chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from Abu Sa'id, from Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding
the person in ihram, if he touches his beard and a hair falls from it, he said: 'He feeds a handful of food or two handfuls.'

key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for accidentally pulling a beard hair while in ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies the fidya for accidentally removing a beard hair while in ihram, prescribing the feeding of one or two handfuls of food. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view on minor accidental breaches of ihram conditions, distinguishing them from intentional violations which carry heavier penalties. The variation between one and two handfuls reflects scholarly discussions on whether the expiation is fixed or dependent on the specific context of the removal.
